sections.title: Integration by Substitution
sections.content: Used when an integrand contains a function and its derivative. Let u = g(x), then du = g'(x)dx. The integral becomes ∫f(u) du. Crucial: For definite integrals, remember to change the limits from x-values to u-values.

sections.title: Integration by Parts & ILATE Rule
sections.content: Used for product of two functions: ∫u*v dx = u*∫v dx - ∫(u' * ∫v dx) dx. Choose the first function (u) based on ILATE preference: Inverse, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential.

sections.title: Partial Fractions
sections.content: Used to integrate rational functions P(x)/Q(x) where degree of P < degree of Q. Factor Q(x) into linear/quadratic terms and split the fraction into simpler parts like A/(x-a) + B/(x-b).

sections.title: Properties of Definite Integrals (King's Rule)
sections.content: The most powerful property (King's Rule): ∫f(x) dx from a to b = ∫f(a + b - x) dx from a to b. It is frequently used to eliminate complex denominators or simplify trigonometric integrals.

sections.title: Even and Odd Functions (Symmetric Limits)
sections.content: For ∫f(x) dx from -a to a: If f(x) is odd (f(-x) = -f(x)), integral is 0. If f(x) is even (f(-x) = f(x)), integral is 2 * ∫f(x) dx from 0 to a.

sections.title: AUC Between Two Curves
sections.content: Area bounded by upper curve y1 and lower curve y2 between x=a and x=b is ∫(y1 - y2) dx. Always find the points of intersection first to determine the exact limits a and b.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting to change the upper and lower limits when using substitution in definite integrals.
2) Choosing the wrong 'u' and 'v' in Integration by Parts, making the integral more complex.
3) Integrating P(x)/Q(x) using partial fractions without first using long division if degree of P >= degree of Q.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 is about standard methods: Substitution, By Parts, Partial Fractions. In definite integrals, Properties (especially King's Rule) heavily reduce calculation. AUC expands to areas bounded between multiple curves.

tricks.title: Classic Exponential Trick
tricks.explanation: ∫e^x * [f(x) + f'(x)] dx is ALWAYS equal to e^x * f(x) + C.

tricks.title: King's Rule Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If applying King's Rule gives an integral I such that I + I leaves only a constant or easily integrable function, the answer is often (b - a)/2 or related.
tricks.example: ∫[sin(x)/(sin(x)+cos(x))] dx from 0 to π/2. I + I = ∫1 dx. 2I = π/2 -> I = π/4.

tricks.title: DI Method (Tabular Integration by Parts)
tricks.explanation: For integrals like ∫x^3 * e^x dx, create a D (Derivatives of x^3) column and an I (Integrals of e^x) column. Alternate signs (+ - + -) and multiply diagonally to get the answer in 10 seconds.

tricks.title: Partial Fraction Cover-Up Method
tricks.explanation: To find A in A/(x-a) + B/(x-b), hide (x-a) in the original fraction and substitute x = a in the remaining part.
tricks.example: For 1/[(x-1)(x-2)] = A/(x-1) + B/(x-2). To find A, hide (x-1) and put x=1 in 1/(x-2) -> A = -1.

tricks.title: f(x) / sqrt(f(x)) Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the numerator is the derivative of the expression inside a square root in the denominator, the integral is 2*sqrt(Denominator).

tricks.title: Shifting Limits Trick
tricks.explanation: ∫f(x) dx from a to b is the exact same as ∫f(x - c) dx from (a+c) to (b+c). Shift limits and function in opposite directions to simplify.
tricks.example: Useful to shift lower limit to 0 for easier limit substitutions.
